Rationale: Default interface property: Path.Combine(GetDirectoryName(ConfigFile) ?? "", "Languages"). Checked ConfigFile without a directory part (gives relative "Languages", CWD-dependent) and invalid chars (GetDirectoryName throws ArgumentException); AppPaths always supplies an absolute ConfigFile so neither occurs in production; follows config.json when PHOTOREVIEW_ISOLATE_CONFIG moves it. Exercised through LocalizationServiceTests (App.Tests).

Default overload ShowBatchReview(IReadOnlyList<BatchReviewItem>) forwards items.Select(Path).ToList() to the path-only overload (drops sizes by design). Null items would NRE (contract violation, callers pass a list). Pure projection, no I/O; covered via FileActionController tests that use the sizes overload.
Lambda item => item.Path inside the default ShowBatchReview forwarder: pure projection of BatchReviewItem.Path; no capture, no null handling needed for a readonly record struct.

VBlankEstimator.Count.get returns _count (0..Capacity=32); single-threaded by contract (WindowsDisplayClock owns one estimator per monitor thread). Asserted indirectly by FewerThanTheMinimumSamples_GiveNoTiming.

Reset sets _count=0,_next=0,Current=null; stale _samples are never read because Sample(index) is bounded by _count. Verified the ring arithmetic after Reset and that DropSamplesBeforeARateChange re-seeds through the same fields. Covered by ARefreshRateChange_IsFollowedWithinAFewRefreshes.

Add ignores timestamp <= previous sample (NonIncreasingTimestamps_AreIgnored), appends in the 32-slot ring, then runs DropSamplesBeforeARateChange and Compute. Ring index math checked for wrap-around. Transient mis-estimate with few samples originates in Compute (see F01346), not here.

Compute uses the lower quartile of the intervals as the one-refresh baseline; with the minimum 4 samples (3 intervals) that is the minimum interval, so a single late wake-up makes it far below one refresh and every other interval is rounded to 2 refreshes. Reproduced: 60 Hz vblanks with one sample 0.4 refresh late, 4 samples -> RefreshPeriod 100000 ticks vs true 166666 (-40 percent). Self-heals as the 32-sample window fills, so transient (Predict kinetic glide). See finding N-core-io-F01.
Sample(index) = _samples[(_next - _count + index + Capacity) % Capacity]: oldest-first mapping verified for _count < Capacity and full ring; always non-negative because _count <= Capacity.

Checked guard _count >= Recent + MinSamples (8) so olderIntervals >= 3 (no divide by zero), the 0.15*nearest tolerance, and the Reset-and-reseed of the last 5 samples (count 5 >= MinSamples, Compute recomputed by Add afterwards). Covered by AnIntegerRatioRateChange_IsFollowedWithinTheSampleWindow.
Default interface no-op Prefetch (test fakes). Production implementer overrides; a no-op cannot affect correctness since TryGetSnapshotProgressiveAsync still queries on demand.

Two-argument TryCopyNew default forwards to the proof overload with a throwaway CopyCreationProof, so callers that do not need ownership proof keep working; no state of its own. PhysicalFileSystem and CountingFileSystem override it explicitly.

Function: IFileSystem.IEnumerable<(string Path, FileStat? Stat)> EnumerateFilesWithStat( string directory, Func<string, bool> include, Action<SkippedEntry> onSkipped)
Rationale: Fake-only default (EnumerateFiles + GetFileStat). Note it stats every file before applying include, unlike PhysicalFileSystem which filters first; all production IFileSystem implementers (PhysicalFileSystem, CountingFileSystem, SlowLinkFileSystem) override it, so no extra production disk reads. onSkipped is never raised by the default (documented).
Lambda path => (path, GetFileStat(path)) in the default EnumerateFilesWithStat: lazily evaluated per element, exceptions surface at enumeration time; used only by fakes.
Lambda f => include(f.path) in the default EnumerateFilesWithStat: include is invoked after the stat (see F01351); null include would NRE at enumeration, callers always pass one.

Function: IFileSystem.bool TryProbeReadable(string path, out string? failure)
Rationale: Default TryProbeReadable returns true with failure=null for in-memory fakes; PhysicalFileSystem overrides. Documented contract (ADR 0007 s3) is honoured by the override, tested in PhysicalIoMutationGapTests.

Function: IFileSystem.IEnumerable<(string Path, FileStat? Stat)> EnumerateReadableFilesWithStat( string directory, Func<string, bool> include, Action<SkippedEntry> onSkipped)
Rationale: Default EnumerateReadableFilesWithStat: ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(onSkipped) runs eagerly (not an iterator), then wraps EnumerateFilesWithStat with a probe filter. Unreadable file is reported once via onSkipped and dropped (ADR 0007 s3). No test for the default itself but PhysicalFileSystem override is covered (EnumerateReadableFilesWithStat_OneFileLocked_...).

Lambda inside default EnumerateReadableFilesWithStat: probe, report SkippedEntry(path, failure ?? "") and return false. failure null guarded with ?? string.Empty; side effect (onSkipped) runs once per enumeration per file.

Default ResolveRealPath = Path.GetFullPath (fakes have no reparse points). PhysicalFileSystem override is the real implementation (see F01919 for its drive-root defect); ActionDestinationPolicy fails closed on IOException.

Begin: ThrowIfNullOrEmpty (interface says must not throw, but this guards programmer error only; callers pass GUID ids), reference-counts under _gate, returns Marker. Thread-safe; covered by LiveOperationMarkerTests.
IsLive returns false for null/empty and tests ContainsKey under _gate; cannot see markers from other processes by design (OS registry does). Covered by LiveOperationMarkerTests.
End decrements or removes under _gate; guards a missing key (double End cannot go negative) and removes at count <= 1. Marker.Dispose uses Interlocked.Exchange so End runs once.
Marker.Dispose is idempotent via Interlocked.Exchange(ref _disposed,1); a second Dispose cannot decrement another handle's count of the same Id.

Test/CLI scheduler: runs the action inline and lets exceptions propagate to the caller (a real Dispatcher would route them to the unhandled-exception handler); null action rejected. Not used in production (Dispatcher-based scheduler is). Covered by ImmediateUiSchedulerTests for the other methods.

InvokeAsync runs inline and converts a throwing action into Task.FromException (RV-S07), matching Dispatcher.InvokeAsync semantics; ArgumentNullException is thrown before the try, so a null action throws synchronously. Tests: InvokeAsync_ActionThrows_ReturnsFaultedTask, _NullAction_Throws.

Function: ImmediateUiScheduler.public async ValueTask YieldAsync(CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
Rationale: YieldAsync throws if the token is already cancelled, then Task.Yield; cancellation after the yield is intentionally not rechecked (same as the real dispatcher yield). No test found for YieldAsync itself (trivial).

Default CanRecycle => true for fakes; the Windows implementation overrides and refuses removable/UNC/unknown volumes (R2-F-05). Checked that the doc'd default cannot leak into production: App wires WindowsRecycleBin.

Default DeletePermanently throws NotSupportedException so a fake that forgot to override cannot silently destroy data; real implementation is only reached after the user enabled and confirmed Q-R8. Covered by PermanentDeleteTests.
Default FitsInRecycleBin => true (fakes). Production override must be false when settings cannot be read (F-WIN-2, ADR 0007 amendment); that logic lives in WindowsRecycleBin, outside this shard.

Function: PhysicalSourceReader.public Stream OpenSource(string path, SourceReadPriority priority, int bufferSize = 1024 * 1024)
Rationale: Opens FileStream(Open, Read, ReadWrite|Delete, bufferSize, SequentialScan); priority ignored by design. bufferSize 0 or 1 means unbuffered, negative throws ArgumentOutOfRange (callers pass 1 MiB). Shares delete so another process may delete/rename while decoding (consistent with OpenReadShared). Covered by SourceReaderSeamMutationTests (Imaging.Tests).
Returns DateTime.UtcNow (Kind=Utc). Test: UtcNowReturnsCurrentUtcDateTime.

Function: AppPaths.public AppPaths(string localAppData, string? dataRootOverride = null, bool isolateConfig = false)
Rationale: Checked: whitespace localAppData throws; override resolved once to a full path; config follows the override only with isolateConfig; journal/sessions/log under override, caches/window placement under the real root unless isolated (the in-code comment saying caches always stay under appRoot is stale for the isolated case, cosmetic). Tests: AppPathsTests (layout, override, isolate, relative, trimmed, invalid).

Blank -> null; Trim + GetFullPath; ArgumentException/NotSupportedException/PathTooLongException -> null so a bad env value cannot crash startup (e.g. NUL). Drive-relative values like "C:" resolve against that drive's CWD (edge, env var is trusted). Tests: InvalidOverride_FallsBackToDefaultRoot, OverrideIsTrimmed, RelativeOverrideIsResolvedOnceToAFullPath.

Single reader of PHOTOREVIEW_DATA_ROOT / PHOTOREVIEW_ISOLATE_CONFIG (enforced by EnvironmentVariableScopeTests); LocalAppData fallback through ResolveLocalAppData. Test: FromEnvironmentReturnsValidInstanceWithAbsolutePaths.
Empty or whitespace LocalApplicationData -> Path.GetTempPath() so a stripped profile cannot throw from a static initializer. Test: ResolveLocalAppData_Empty_UsesTempPath.

Accepts "1" or "true" (case-insensitive) after Trim, ordinal compare; null false. Anything else (including "yes") is false, which only fails safe (config not isolated -> tests would touch real config, guarded separately by DataRootFixtureConfigIsolationTests).

Function: BoundedLruCache.public BoundedLruCache(long capacity, Func<TValue, long> sizeOf, IEqualityComparer<TKey>? comparer = null)
Rationale: capacity <= 0 throws; sizeOf null throws; comparer null falls back to default. Cache holds no unmanaged resources so no disposal contract needed. Tests: BoundedLruCacheTests (capacity enforcement).
Count read under _gate; consistent with _items. Used for diagnostics only.
CurrentSize read under _gate; always the sum of resident entry sizes (maintained in Set/RemoveCore/Clear). Test: LruEnforcesByteCapacity.

Function: BoundedLruCache.public bool TryGet(TKey key, [MaybeNullWhen(false)] out TValue value)
Rationale: TryGet moves the node to the front under _gate and returns the stored value; no value copy outside lock needed (values are immutable decoded images / byte[]). MaybeNotNull annotation satisfied (value=default on miss). Tests: LruRetainsRecentlyAccessedEntry.

Function: BoundedLruCache.public void Set(TKey key, TValue value)
Rationale: Checked: size = Math.Max(1, sizeOf) so zero/negative sizes cannot disable eviction; replacement removes the old entry first even when the new value is oversize (OversizeReplacementDropsStaleEntry); eviction loop terminates because size <= capacity; sizeOf throwing leaves state untouched (called before the lock). Overflow of _size + size only if capacity is near long.MaxValue (not used). Evicted values are not disposed (IDecodedImage is not IDisposable).
Remove delegates to RemoveCore under _gate; returns false for a missing key. Covered indirectly by PreviewImageService invalidation tests (Imaging.Tests); no direct Core test found.

Predicate runs under _gate over a ToArray snapshot, so a throwing predicate removes nothing and the dictionary is never mutated during enumeration; null predicate rejected (RemoveWhereNullPredicateThrows). A slow predicate would hold the cache lock (callers use cheap path predicates).
Clear empties dictionary, list and size under one lock. No test found for Clear in BoundedLruCacheTests (trivial body).
Dictionary.Remove(key, out node) then LinkedList.Remove(node) and _size -= node size; the node is owned by this list so Remove cannot throw. Callers hold _gate.

Function: ForwardedOpenCoalescer.public ForwardedOpenCoalescer(Action<string?> open, TimeSpan window, ILog? log = null, Func<TimeSpan, CancellationToken, Task>? delay = null)
Rationale: Null open rejected, window stored as-is (a negative/zero window just makes Task.Delay throw or complete, which FlushAfterWindowAsync handles), log defaults to NullLog. Tests: ForwardingCoreTests, Coalescer_WindowDelayFails_IsLoggedAndTheOpenStillHappens.

Under _gate: ignored after Dispose; while a window is pending the first non-null path wins (_first ??= first), a path-less request still triggers one open; new window started outside the lock. Tests: Coalescer_BurstOfLaunches_OpensFirstPathOnce, _SeparateBursts_AreSeparateOpens, _Submit_DoesNotRunOrWaitForTheOpenCallback.

OperationCanceledException (Dispose) exits without opening; any other delay failure is logged and the open still happens; _pending reset under the lock before _open so a Submit during the open starts a new window; _open exceptions logged. Race: Dispose between the lock and _open can still fire one open (harmless, App posts to a closing UI). Tests: Coalescer_Dispose_CancelsPendingOpen, Coalescer_OpenCallbackThrows_IsLoggedAndTheNextSubmitStillWorks.
Sets _disposed under the lock then cancels the CTS (CTS itself is not disposed, no timers attached so nothing leaks). Idempotent. Test: Coalescer_Dispose_CancelsPendingOpen.

Checked: count > 16, any path failing IsAcceptablePath (shared contract with the decoder), strict UTF-8 (lone surrogates rejected earlier), total size cap 64 KiB. A null element would throw NullReferenceException instead of ArgumentException (contract violation; callers filter with File.Exists). Tests: Encode_ExactlyMaxPaths..., Protocol_Encode_RejectsWhatDecodeWouldReject, Encode_PathWithLoneSurrogate_ThrowsArgumentException.

True only for length >= 2 ending in two LF bytes; header-only message "H\n\n" is complete; a path list cannot contain an empty line so the terminator is unambiguous. Test: IsComplete_OnlyAMessageEndingWithAnEmptyLineIsComplete.

Function: ForwardedPathProtocol.public static bool TryDecode(ReadOnlySpan<byte> message, Func<string, bool> pathExists, out IReadOnlyList<string> paths)
Rationale: Untrusted-input parser: size cap, terminator, strict UTF-8 (BOM and invalid bytes rejected), header, <= 16 paths, per-path shape plus pathExists; CRLF rejected through IsControl; any failure returns false with paths=[]. pathExists is called on attacker-chosen strings (UNC could trigger an SMB lookup) but the pipe is CurrentUserOnly. Tests: ForwardedPathProtocolLimitTests (18), Protocol_RejectsHostilePrefixes_EvenIfExists.

Checked: empty/over-long, control chars, unpaired surrogates, device/extended prefixes in all separator spellings (\\?\, //?/, \??\, \\.\), ".." segments, IsPathFullyQualified. "..." segments are not parent traversal on Windows (verified Path.GetFullPath keeps them). Pattern precedence (p[2] is ? or .) parses as intended. Tests: Path_DeviceOrExtendedNamespace_IsRejectedByEncodeAndDecode, Path_TwoSeparators_NeverCrashesTheShapeCheck.
Trivial separator predicate for \ and /.

Rune.DecodeFromUtf16 loop with OperationStatus.Done; consumed advances correctly for pairs; invalid lone high/low surrogate returns false. Tests: Encode_ValidSurrogatePair_RoundTrips, Encode_PathWithLoneSurrogate_ThrowsArgumentException.

Function: SecondInstanceHandoff.public static async Task<bool> TryForwardAsync( IInstanceForwardClient client, IReadOnlyList<string> existingPaths, TimeSpan timeout, ILog? log = null, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
Rationale: Non-cancellation client exceptions are swallowed into false (caller falls back to opening locally); OCE rethrown (the shipped client maps its own timeout to Unknown/NoInstance, so only caller cancellation escapes); Delivered/Unknown -> true per Q-R12 (accepted trade-off). Null existingPaths would NRE only after a successful send (callers pass a list). Tests: Handoff_ExitsOnlyWhenTheOwnerTookOrLikelyTookTheRequest, TryForward_*.
Counts one stat then forwards; counter increments even when inner throws (intended: the query was issued). Test: StatQueriesAreCounted.
Same as FileExists: RecordStat then forward. Test: StatQueriesAreCounted.
RecordStat then forward; return value unchanged. Test: StatQueriesAreCounted.

Function: CountingFileSystem.public void Move(string source, string destination)
Rationale: Pure forwarder, not counted (OtherOperationsAreNotCounted); exceptions propagate unchanged.

Function: CountingFileSystem.public void Copy(string source, string destination)
Rationale: Pure forwarder; exceptions propagate unchanged.

Function: CountingFileSystem.public bool TryCopyNew(string source, string destination)
Rationale: Two-argument forwarder to _inner.TryCopyNew(source, destination); no proof is exposed here, which is correct because callers needing proof use the three-argument overload (N-core-io-005).
Pure forwarder to _inner.Delete (not counted as a stat, per OtherOperationsAreNotCounted); IOException/UnauthorizedAccess propagate unchanged.

Function: CountingFileSystem.public Stream OpenReadShared(string path, int bufferSize = 65536)
Rationale: Forwards path and bufferSize; stream ownership passes to the caller.

Function: CountingFileSystem.public Stream OpenAppend(string path, bool durable)
Rationale: Forwards durable flag unchanged (journal durability mode must not be altered by the decorator).

Function: CountingFileSystem.public void WriteAllTextAtomic(string path, string text, bool durable = true)
Rationale: Forwards durable flag; default durable=true preserved. Wrapper cannot weaken atomicity.
Pure forwarder to _inner.ReadAllText; not counted and no caching, so SettingsStore retry logic sees the original IOException.

Function: CountingFileSystem.public IEnumerable<string> EnumerateFiles(string directory, string pattern = "*")
Rationale: Forwards directory and pattern lazily (returns the inner enumerable).

Function: CountingFileSystem.public IEnumerable<(string Path, FileStat? Stat)> EnumerateFilesWithStat(string directory, Func<string, bool> include, Action<SkippedEntry> onSkipped)
Rationale: Forwards to inner fast listing; stat from the directory entry is not counted (no extra I/O), consistent with the class doc.

Function: CountingFileSystem.public bool TryProbeReadable(string path, out string? failure)
Rationale: Forwards TryProbeReadable including the out parameter.

Function: CountingFileSystem.public IEnumerable<(string Path, FileStat? Stat)> EnumerateReadableFilesWithStat(string directory, Func<string, bool> include, Action<SkippedEntry> onSkipped)
Rationale: Forwards to inner EnumerateReadableFilesWithStat so the physical override's probe/skip logic is kept; if the decorator relied on the interface default the wrapper's own TryProbeReadable would be used, which also forwards.
Forwarder to _inner.EnumerateDirectories; returns the inner lazy enumerable, so errors surface at enumeration time exactly as for PhysicalFileSystem.
Forwarder to _inner.CreateDirectory (idempotent, creates parents); not counted as a stat; exceptions unchanged.
Forwards ResolveRealPath so the security check sees the physical implementation, not the interface default (verified: otherwise containment would silently degrade to Path.GetFullPath).

Recognises only IOException whose HResult is Win32 facility with code 80 or 183 (checked masks 0xFFFF and 0x7FFF0000 against 0x80070050/0x800700B7; the negative int HResult is handled). Non-IO exceptions with the same HResult are rejected. Tests: IsDestinationExists_OnlyWin32FileExistsAndAlreadyExists_AreRecognized, IsDestinationExists_NonIoExceptionWithTheSameHResult_IsNotRecognized.

Function: NavigationStatWorker.public Task<T> RunAsync<T>(Func<T> work, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
Rationale: Enqueue is correct (pre-cancelled token short-circuits, work exceptions fault only that task). Suspect: one FIFO thread with no per-item timeout, and a token cancelled AFTER enqueue is only honoured at dequeue, so a stalled SMB stat blocks every later navigation stat (even after switching to a local folder) and cancelled awaiters stay pending until it returns. Documented intent is only to keep the UI thread free. Not reproduced (needs a stalled share). Tests cover pre-cancelled and queued-cancel only. See finding N-core-io-F05.

Local Execute: re-checks the token at dequeue (no disk touch for superseded items), result and exceptions routed to TaskCompletionSource so the worker loop never throws; an OperationCanceledException thrown by work becomes a faulted (not cancelled) task, which await still surfaces as OCE. Test: StatWorker_ItemCancelledWhileQueued_IsCancelledWithoutRunningItsWork.

Loop dequeues under _gate with Monitor.Wait/Pulse (no lost wake-up: queue count re-checked, thread started lazily under the same lock); background thread, AboveNormal priority. Single-thread stall behaviour is recorded under F01891.

ThrowIfNullOrWhiteSpace then File.Exists (never throws for bad paths, returns false; directories give false). Whitespace path throws instead of returning false (fail-loud, callers pass catalog paths). Test: FileExistsReturnsTrueWhenPresentAndFalseWhenMissing.
Directory.Exists with the same argument guard; files give false. Test: DirectoryExistsReturnsTrueWhenPresentAndFalseWhenMissing.

new FileInfo(path): Exists then Length/LastWriteTimeUtc come from one cached attribute fetch, so no TOCTOU between Exists and Length; directories give null. Test: GetFileStatReturnsMetadataForExistingFileAndNullForMissing.

Function: PhysicalFileSystem.public void Move(string source, string destination)
Rationale: File.Move without overwrite: destination collision throws (Move_DestinationExists_ThrowsAndKeepsBoth, case-only collision too); cross-volume move is copy+delete inside the OS (not atomic) which FileActionService handles with its own journal/ownership logic. File.Move would also move a directory if source became one (TOCTOU only, source stat-verified earlier).

Function: PhysicalFileSystem.public void Copy(string source, string destination)
Rationale: File.Copy without overwrite: throws if destination exists and keeps both (Copy_DestinationExists_ThrowsAndKeepsBoth); source untouched. A failure after creation can leave a partial destination (caller must prove ownership via TryCopyNew proof).

Function: PhysicalFileSystem.public bool TryCopyNew(string source, string destination)
Rationale: Two-argument overload creates a throwaway proof and delegates to the proof overload (N-core-io-004); semantics identical. Tests: PhysicalFileSystemTryCopyNewTests.

Thin wrapper over FileSystemErrors.IsDestinationExists kept for test access; only Win32 80/183 IOExceptions are swallowed, everything else rethrown. Test: IsSwallowedAsDestinationExists_EveryOtherFailure_IsRethrown.

File.Delete: missing file is a silent success (idempotent, DeleteRemovesFileAndIsIdempotentOnMissingFile); directory path throws UnauthorizedAccessException; callers only delete operation-owned temp/partial files (ownership proof lives in the callers). Delete does not follow reparse links.

Function: PhysicalFileSystem.public Stream OpenReadShared(string path, int bufferSize = 65536)
Rationale: Open/Read with ReadWrite|Delete share and SequentialScan; negative bufferSize throws, 0/1 unbuffered. Missing file throws FileNotFoundException (callers classify). Test: OpenReadSharedAllowsReadingEntireContent.

Function: PhysicalFileSystem.public Stream OpenAppend(string path, bool durable)
Rationale: FileMode.Append + FileShare.Read: single writer at a time (second process gets a sharing violation, journal retries via AppendAttempts); WriteThrough only when durable (ADR 0007). Does not create the parent directory (OperationJournal creates it first). Torn-tail handling is the journal reader's job. Tests: OpenAppendAppendsSequentially, OperationJournalDurableFlushTests.

Function: PhysicalFileSystem.public void WriteAllTextAtomic(string path, string text, bool durable = true)
Rationale: Checked: temp name path + GUID + .tmp in the same directory (same-volume rename), CreateNew + FileShare.None so only this call's file is ever deleted in finally; flush(durable) before the rename; UTF-8 without BOM; original untouched on any failure (Save_WriteFails_KeepsPreviousFileAndState, WriteAllTextAtomic_RenameFails_LeavesNoTempFile). Directory entry is not fsynced (acceptable: atomicity, not durability of the rename, ADR 0007). Orphan temp after a process crash is swept only for sessions (SessionStore), not for config.json (a few KB, cosmetic).

Function: PhysicalFileSystem.private static void ReplaceWithRetry(string tempPath, string path)
Rationale: Binds File.Move(temp, path, overwrite:true) and Thread.Sleep to the testable overload; same-directory replace. Covered through WriteAllTextAtomic tests and ReplaceWithRetryTests.
Lambda () => File.Move(tempPath, path, overwrite: true): MoveFileEx REPLACE_EXISTING on same volume; throws IOException/UnauthorizedAccess on contention, which the retry wrapper classifies.

static delay => Thread.Sleep(delay): blocks the calling thread up to 3+6+...+21 = 84 ms in total (settings save on UI thread is bounded). Test: SharingViolation_RetriedThenSucceeds uses the injected sleeper.

Function: PhysicalFileSystem.internal static void ReplaceWithRetry(Action move, Action<int> sleep)
Rationale: Retries only transient failures (sharing 32, lock 33, UnauthorizedAccess) up to 8 attempts, the last attempt rethrows the original exception; non-transient surfaces at once. Tests: SharingViolation_RetriedThenSucceeds, AccessDenied_RetriedThenRethrown, NonTransient_SurfacesImmediately.

Matches UnauthorizedAccessException or IOException with HResult 0x80070020/0x80070021 (unchecked int constants correct). A genuinely read-only target is also UnauthorizedAccess and is retried ~84 ms before surfacing (accepted, bounded).

File.ReadAllText (UTF-8 with BOM detection, FileShare.Read): a writer-held file fails with IOException which SettingsStore retries; loads the whole file in memory (config/session only). Test: WriteAllTextAtomicAndReadAllTextRoundTrip, Load_Utf8Bom_KeepsValues.

Function: PhysicalFileSystem.public IEnumerable<string> EnumerateFiles(string directory, string pattern = "*")
Rationale: Directory.EnumerateFiles(directory, pattern ?? "*"): lazy, errors at enumeration time; default MatchType is Simple so no legacy 8.3 extension quirk. Test: EnumerateFilesMatchesPatternAndRespectsTopDirectoryOnly.

Function: PhysicalFileSystem.public IEnumerable<(string Path, FileStat? Stat)> EnumerateReadableFilesWithStat( string directory, Func<string, bool> include, Action<SkippedEntry> onSkipped)
Rationale: Iterator chaining EnumerateFilesWithStat and TryProbeReadable; onSkipped null check is deferred to the first MoveNext (iterator) rather than the call, which only changes where a programmer error surfaces. Unreadable files are reported once and skipped (ADR 0007 s3). Test: EnumerateReadableFilesWithStat_OneFileLocked_IsSkippedAndReportedWhileTheOthersAreListed.

Function: PhysicalFileSystem.public bool TryProbeReadable(string path, out string? failure)
Rationale: One open/close with ReadWrite|Delete share, buffer 1, never reads bytes; IOException/UnauthorizedAccessException become false plus the OS message, other exceptions propagate. A file deleted between listing and probe is also reported as unreadable (FileNotFound is an IOException), which is informative rather than wrong. Tests: TryProbeReadable_* in PhysicalIoMutationGapTests, FileSystemContractTests.

Function: PhysicalFileSystem.public IEnumerable<(string Path, FileStat? Stat)> EnumerateFilesWithStat( string directory, Func<string, bool> include, Action<SkippedEntry> onSkipped)
Rationale: Public fast listing delegates to the test-seam overload with DirectoryInfo.EnumerateFiles("*"); no per-file open (AR16). Tests: SkippedKindTests.FastListing_DoesNotProbe_LockedFileIsListed_AndTheProbeReportsIt.

static dir => new DirectoryInfo(dir).EnumerateFiles("*").GetEnumerator(): lazy; DirectoryNotFound/UnauthorizedAccess surfaces on the first MoveNext (propagates, see F01916). Test: EnumerateFilesWithStat_FolderDoesNotExist_Propagates.

Function: PhysicalFileSystem.internal static IEnumerable<(string Path, FileStat? Stat)> EnumerateFilesWithStat( string directory, Func<string, bool> include, Action<SkippedEntry> onSkipped, Func<string, IEnumerator<FileInfo>> openListing)
Rationale: Failure before the first entry propagates (loud), failure after listed > 0 (IOException or UnauthorizedAccess) is reported as ListingInterrupted and keeps the partial catalog (ADR 0007 s3), non-IO exceptions propagate; filter precedence "listed > 0 && ex is A or B" parses correctly; include/Length/LastWriteTimeUtc come from the directory entry. Argument checks are lazy (iterator). Tests: PhysicalFileSystemListingInterruptedTests (4).
Directory.EnumerateDirectories lazy; guard on null/whitespace. Test: EnumerateDirectoriesListsImmediateSubdirectories.
Directory.CreateDirectory is idempotent and creates parents; throws IOException if a file occupies the name. Used by Save paths, covered by Save_CreatesTheConfigDirectoryBeforeWriting.

Segment walk follows junctions/symlinks including final segment (chained junction through a second junction verified to resolve to the real target, so containment is sound), but for a drive-root input the loop has no segments and returns root.TrimEnd = "C:" (drive-relative, CWD-dependent) instead of "C:\". Reproduced: ResolveRealPath("C:\") -> "C:". Masked today because ActionDestinationPolicy trims and re-appends a separator, but the contract says absolute path. UNC root similar. See finding N-core-io-F02.

Uses Directory.Exists/File.Exists then LinkTarget/ResolveLinkTarget(returnFinalTarget:true); a non-link reparse point (OneDrive placeholder, volume mount) has null LinkTarget and is left as-is (acceptable: not a redirect the user did not choose); loops/unreadable targets throw IOException which ActionDestinationPolicy treats as an escape (fail closed). Tests: PhysicalIoJunctionNativeTests, PhysicalFileSystemReparseTests.

FileShare.Read|Delete denies writers (appenders get a sharing violation and retry) while allowing readers and the POSIX rename; throws IOException when a writer holds the file now. Test: OpenReadDenyWriters_BlocksAppendOpens_AllowsCompatibleReaders.

CreateFileW CREATE_NEW with GENERIC_WRITE|DELETE and share Read: an existing temp file throws IOException (HResult kept) and is never touched (CreateStagedReplacement_FileAlreadyExists_...); handle disposed on failure; GetHRForLastWin32Error read before Dispose. Very unlikely leak: FileStream ctor failure would leave the handle and a created temp until the next compaction sweep. No long-path prefix (journal lives under LocalAppData).
Writes bytes through the 64 KiB-buffered FileStream; no length or disposal guard (ObjectDisposedException comes from FileStream). Compaction caller owns ordering.
FileStream.Flush(flushToDisk:true) = FlushFileBuffers, handle opened GENERIC_WRITE so permitted; independent of journal durability mode as documented.

FILE_RENAME_INFO layout checked for x64/x86 (flags at 0, RootDirectory at pointer size, FileNameLength, FileName; buffer includes terminator), FILE_RENAME_INFO_EX class 22 with REPLACE_IF_EXISTS|POSIX_SEMANTICS; flushes first; unmanaged buffer freed in finally; _replaced set only after success so a failed rename leaves target unchanged and Dispose deletes the temp. Tests: ReplaceAtomically_* (3 cases incl. appender-held failure).

Idempotent dispose: closes the stream (final flush IOException swallowed because the file is deleted anyway), deletes the temp only when not replaced, tolerating IOException/UnauthorizedAccess (next compaction removes leftovers). Test: Dispose_WithoutReplace_DeletesTempFile, StagedReplacementDispose_LeftoverTempThatCannotBeDeleted_DoesNotThrow.
Default ctor composes AppPaths.FromEnvironment and PhysicalFileSystem, used by the fallback in ImagePresenter/MainViewModel; no logic of its own.

Function: SessionStore.public SessionStore(IAppPaths paths, IFileSystem fileSystem, ReviewMetrics? metrics = null)
Rationale: Argument checks; starts the stale-temp sweep on a pool task (R14) so the UI thread is not blocked; sweep failures other than IO/UnauthorizedAccess would only fault the unobserved StartupSweepTask (harmless). Tests: Constructor_NullValidation, Constructor_SweepsStaleTempFiles, SessionStoreSweepPerfTests.
Lambda () => SweepStaleTempFiles(DateTime.UtcNow) on Task.Run: captures this only; safe against concurrent Save/Load because the 1-day age guard never touches a live temp file.
static () => FileLog.Default test seam; Log() is wrapped in try/catch by the callers so a throwing logger cannot break Load/Save (Save_WriteFailsAndLoggerThrows_StillDoesNotThrow).

Deletes only *.tmp files in the Sessions folder older than one day (exact one-day boundary kept: SweepStaleTempFiles_TempExactlyOneDayOld_IsKeptAndOlderOneIsRemoved); per-file try/catch so one locked file does not stop the rest; enumeration IO/UnauthorizedAccess returns 0. Clock skew only delays deletion.

Malformed folder (NUL, overlong) -> empty session; missing, empty, corrupt or NUL-filled file -> empty session with a warning (JsonException) per ADR 0007 s2; IO/UnauthorizedAccess also yield an empty session silently (no log; next Save would overwrite an unreadable file, accepted best-effort). null Skipped normalised, blank Folder repaired. Tests: SessionStoreTests (Load_*), SessionStoreLogTests, SessionWritePolicyTests.SessionLoad_EmptyOrPartialFile_ReturnsNoSession.

Atomic non-durable write (ADR 0007 s2) inside a catch for IO/UnauthorizedAccess/ArgumentException/NotSupported/InvalidOperation, logging failures without throwing; the ThrowIfNullOrWhiteSpace(state.Folder) sits outside the try on purpose (programmer error). Lone-surrogate folder names fail serialization and are logged, not written. Tests: Save_UnexpectedFileSystemFailure_DoesNotThrow, SessionSave_UsesNonDurableAtomicWrite.

SHA-256 of the upper-cased canonical folder, one file per folder; stable file-name scheme pinned by GetPath_KeepsThePersistedFileNameScheme; relative input resolves against CWD (callers pass full paths). Mapped drive vs UNC spellings give different sessions (accepted).

GetFullPath, then trims trailing separators except for a drive root (C:\ keeps its slash, so root and child differ). Tests: CanonicalFolder_TrimsTrailingSeparatorsExceptOnADriveRoot, GetPath_FolderWithAndWithoutTrailingSeparator_IsTheSameFile....

Function: SessionWriter.public SessionWriter(SessionStore store, ILog? log = null, TimeSpan? debounce = null, Func<TimeSpan, CancellationToken, Task>? delay = null)
Rationale: Constructor does not validate debounce. Negative debounce (other than -1 ms): Task.Delay throws inside RunTimerAsync, _timerCts is never cleared, so every later Update returns early and nothing is written until Flush/Dispose (reproduced: no file after 500 ms, WhenIdleAsync faulted, written only after Flush). Production always uses DefaultDebounce (500 ms) so this is latent. See finding N-core-io-F03.

Update starts RunTimerAsync while holding _gate; when the injected delay or a zero debounce completes synchronously, the continuation runs on the caller thread and WritePending (file write) executes inside the _gate lock (reproduced with debounce=0: file exists when Update returns). Latent (default 500 ms). Snapshot copy, version bump and disposed check are correct. See finding N-core-io-F03.

Canonical folder as key, falling back to the raw string on ArgumentException/NotSupportedException/PathTooLongException so a malformed folder cannot throw from Update/Flush. Test: Update_FolderThatCannotBeCanonicalised_DoesNotThrowAndOtherFoldersAreStillWritten, Update_TrailingSeparatorVariants_NewestWins.

Public Flush is the bounded variant (UI folder change must not hang behind another writer); semantics covered by FlushWritesImmediatelyAndOnlyOnce and Flush_WriterBusy_ReturnsAfterBoundedWaitAndRequeues. Stall inside the caller's own save is not bounded (see F02032).

Clears _timerCts under the gate, cancels the timer then drains; the timer task that already passed its delay re-checks ReferenceEquals(_timerCts, cts) so no double write. CTS is not disposed (no unmanaged resource).
Task.Run(Flush) uses the bounded path; exceptions inside Flush are not expected (WriteBatch catches Save errors).
Returns the most recent timer task under _gate (tests and shutdown only); an older superseded timer is not awaited.

Marks disposed under the gate, bounded flush, then waits at most ShutdownWait minus elapsed for drained-but-unwritten batches; deliberately keeps _writeLock undisposed (R2-A-04). Late Updates are ignored silently. A bounded flush that times out while disposed drops the requeue (logged as writer busy). Tests: Dispose_* (6) in SessionWriterTests and SessionWriterShutdownAndVersionTests.

Waits on Monitor under _gate until _inFlight reaches 0 or the deadline, logs an error and returns on timeout (negative remaining handled), PulseAll in WritePending finally wakes it. Tests: Dispose_WriteStuckLongerThanShutdownWait_GivesUpAfterTheBoundIncludingTimeAlreadySpent.

Only OperationCanceledException is handled around the injected delay: any other exception (e.g. ArgumentOutOfRange from a negative debounce) leaves _timerCts set permanently, so Update never schedules again and the latest state is written only by Flush/Dispose; the faulted task is never observed. After a successful delay it correctly clears _timerCts under the lock and writes unbounded. Reproduced for the negative-debounce case. See finding N-core-io-F03.

Drains _pending with the version of each key under the gate and increments _inFlight only for a non-empty batch; finally decrements and PulseAll even if WriteBatch throws. Test: WriteBatch_NonIoException_DoesNotDropRestOfBatch, Dispose_WhileTimerHoldsDrainedBatch_StillWritesIt.

Lambda pair => (pair.Value, version) captures nothing but _versions under the lock; missing version yields 0 which cannot equal a live version (>=1) so a never-updated key would be skipped, not mis-written.

Function: SessionWriter.private void RequeueSkipped(List<(SessionState State, long Version)> batch)
Rationale: Re-adds a skipped batch only when the key's version is unchanged and TryAdd does not overwrite a newer pending snapshot; returns when disposed (shutdown loses it, logged by caller). Does not restart the timer, so a requeued state waits for the next Update/Flush (acceptable: folder switch is followed by an Update). Test: Flush_TimedOutBatchWhoseStateWasSuperseded_IsNotRequeuedOverTheNewerState.

Function: SessionWriter.private void WriteBatch(List<(SessionState State, long Version)> batch, bool bounded)
Rationale: Bounded mode only bounds the wait for _writeLock; once acquired, _store.Save runs synchronously on the calling thread, so a save that stalls after the lock is free (NAS/disk hang) blocks UI-thread Flush() and Dispose beyond the 2 s budget (Q-R5 intent). Version check and per-item catch are otherwise correct. Known audit candidate; fix is in open PR #296 (not merged on master). Traced and confirmed by that PR's author test; not reproduced here. See finding N-core-io-F04.

JSON round trip through AppSettingsJsonContext (same contract as disk): copies every property incl. ones a UI forgets. Checked a NaN/Infinity double would throw ArgumentException at Serialize (Normalize resets NaN on load; UI-side finite check is R05b, App shard). Null Actions/Shortcuts round-trip as null. Test: EveryPublicSettingRoundTripsThroughClone, Fuzz_NormalizeIdempotent_CloneEqual.

Four default actions with localized names via Tr (names are fixed at creation time, so a later language switch does not rename saved actions; cosmetic); destinations are language-neutral folder names. Test: Defaults_NamesAreLocalized_FoldersAreNeutral.

Function: SettingsLoadRepairText.public static string Build(IReadOnlyList<string> repairs, bool forImport = false)
Rationale: Splits repairs by the "Shortcuts." prefix (ordinal): resets use one line (config vs import wording), disabled shortcuts one line each with the prefix stripped; "Actions[i].Shortcut" repair names go to the reset line. Null list rejected. Tests: Build_* (4) in SettingsStoreLoadRepairPersistenceTests.
Lambda r => !r.StartsWith("Shortcuts.", Ordinal) selects reset names; complement of F02037, so every repair appears in exactly one group.
Lambda r => r.StartsWith("Shortcuts.", Ordinal) selects disabled-shortcut entries; ordinal comparison per AGENTS.md CA1310 rule.

Checked each numeric/enum repair: <=0 capacity, RAM percent clamp, worker count clamp, load limit NaN-safe (!(x>0 && x<=1)), preload counts, undefined enums, LibRaw backend, null actions, blank mandatory shortcuts (RV-S03 clears a clashing action shortcut), mouse/toolbar/font/transition ranges. R05 fixed on master (non-finite font size reset to 12, keyboard zoom step clamped; NonFiniteAndZoomStepSettingsTests). Not repaired: duplicate mandatory shortcuts (left to the validator), UiLanguage and string paths. Tests: SettingsNormalizerMutationGapTests plus per-setting test files.
Lambda a => a is null for RemoveAll: removes explicit null entries so later foreach does not NRE; count drives the Actions repair report.

Takes every mandatory shortcut plus all action shortcuts, then resolves optional shortcuts in OptionalNames order (earlier wins, later disabled and reported); modifier-only differences (Ctrl+O vs O) are conservatively treated as clashes, same as the validator. Reflection-based property lookup throws InvalidOperationException only if OptionalNames is out of sync (guarded by tests). Tests: ViewerQuickSettingsTests.DisableConflictingOptionalShortcuts_* (6), DisableConflictingOptionalShortcuts_AliasOfActionKey_Disabled.
Local Take adds the canonical key when non-blank; null-safe for action?.Shortcut.
Local Resolve canonicalises, returns "" for blank, reports and blanks a key already taken, otherwise claims it; HashSet.Add result used correctly.
Repairs property: ResetSettings followed by "Shortcuts."+name for each disabled shortcut (order documented and used by LastLoadRepairs); recomputed on each access (cheap, small lists).
Lambda name => "Shortcuts." + name in the Repairs projection: invariant string concat, no culture involved.

Returns _current (non-volatile field, written on the UI thread by Load/Save; readers on other threads may see a stale reference, benign because AppSettings instances are replaced, not mutated, by Save).

Function: SettingsStore.public SettingsStore( IAppPaths appPaths, IFileSystem fileSystem, ILog log, Action<string, Exception>? onStartupError = null, IKeyNameValidator? keyNameValidator = null)
Rationale: All dependencies null-checked, permissive SimpleKeyNameValidator fallback, builds SettingsValidator. Tests: Constructor_CustomKeyNameValidator_IsExposedAndUsedForShortcutValidation, Constructor_NoValidator_FallsBackToAnyNonBlankName.
Delegates to SettingsValidator with this store's key validator (replaced the process-wide static, AR11a).
Permissive fallback validator: any non-blank name is valid (production wires WpfKeyNameValidator). Test: Constructor_NoValidator_FallsBackToAnyNonBlankName.

Retries IOException/UnauthorizedAccessException up to 4 times (50/100/200/400 ms, 750 ms worst case on the startup thread) then rethrows; a file deleted mid-way is also an IOException and exhausts the retries before the caller degrades to in-memory defaults. Tests: Load_TransientReadFailure_IsRetriedAndLogged, Load_TransientReadFailure_IsRetried.

Data-safety paths verified (corrupt file backed up before defaults, backup collision/failure sets _keepCorruptFile so the only copy is never overwritten, newer-version files not rewritten, locked file keeps in-memory defaults, Changed raised outside the try). Issue: repairs produced only by SettingsNormalizer (clamped/reset values) or optional-shortcut disabling are persisted over config.json by TryPersistRepairs WITHOUT a backup (only the salvage path backs up), so the user's original out-of-range values are permanently replaced; the dialog names the settings but not the old values. Traced; tests (Load_RepairIsPersistedExactlyOnce...) assert the rewrite, none asserts a backup. See finding N-core-io-F06.

Persists repairs and converts IOException/UnauthorizedAccessException into false plus a startup error (repairs stay in memory); other exceptions would propagate, but Normalize now guarantees serializable values (R05). Tests: Load_RepairThatCannotBePersisted_StillLoadsAndReportsTheRepair.

Honors _keepCorruptFile (memory-only, logged), creates the directory, canonicalises shortcuts in place, stamps ConfigVersion, durable atomic write; serialization of a NaN/Infinity double throws ArgumentException before any write (reproduced: config.json not created), so a bad value can never produce a partial file. No validation here by design (UI calls ValidateShortcuts). Concurrent saves from two processes are last-writer-wins, never torn (ConcurrentSaveAndLoad_NeverTorn). Tests: Save_WriteFails_KeepsPreviousFileAndState, Save_WritesAtomicAndRaisesChanged.

Function: SettingsStore.private static bool TrySalvage(string json, out AppSettings settings, out IReadOnlyList<string> unusable)
Rationale: Property-by-property recovery using JsonDocument (comments/trailing commas allowed, same as the context); non-object root returns false so the caller treats the file as corrupt; per-property JsonException/NotSupported/InvalidOperation skip only that property. Granularity is top-level: one bad element inside Actions resets the whole Actions list (documented by Load_BadElementInsideActions_ResetsOnlyActions, original kept as .corrupt backup).
Lambda p => string.Equals(p.Name, element.Name, Ordinal): case-sensitive, matching the case-sensitive main deserializer, so salvage cannot accept a spelling the normal path rejects.

Backup name .corrupt-yyyyMMddHHmmss (invariant culture) with -2..-99 suffixes; if all taken, the last candidate exists and File.Copy throws, which the callers treat as backup failure (keep corrupt file). Tests: Load_CorruptConfigWithFirstBackupNameTaken_UsesTheSecondName, ..._EveryBackupNameTaken_UsesTheLastNumberedNameBelowOneHundred.

Function: SettingsStore.private void LogStartupError(string message, Exception ex)
Rationale: Routes startup errors to the optional UI callback or the log; a throwing callback would propagate (UI callback is App-owned).

Internal test seam: Deserialize ?? new AppSettings then FinishDeserialize; no normalise/salvage by design (public path is ParseText). Fixture tests Parse_V1Fixture_MigratesProperly, Parse_V2Fixture_ParsesCorrectly.

Single parse pipeline for Load and Import: deserialize, salvage on JsonException, legacy marker, migrate, normalise, disable conflicting optional shortcuts; non-object text throws JsonException; JSON null flagged for Import. NaN/Infinity string input verified to be reset to 12 with a repair name. Tests: SettingsParseTextTests (12), ParseTextAndLoad_SameFileText_GiveIdenticalSettingsAndRepairs.

Function: SettingsStore.private static void FinishDeserialize(AppSettings loaded, string json)
Rationale: Order matters and is right: legacy marker before Migrate, then null Shortcuts/Actions defaulted. Re-parses the JSON once more for the marker (negligible cost).

Function: SettingsStore.private static void MarkUnversionedAsLegacy(AppSettings loaded, string json)
Rationale: Peeks the raw JSON for a missing ConfigVersion key (case-sensitive, consistent with the deserializer) and forces version 1 so migrations run (Q-L1); unparseable JSON leaves the value alone. Side effect on explicit UiLanguage is in Migrate (F02061). Tests: ParseText_NoConfigVersionKey_IsTreatedAsLegacyAndMigrated, Load_ConfigWithoutVersionKey_KeepsVietnamese.

ConfigVersion < 3 unconditionally sets UiLanguage = "vi", even when the text explicitly contains another UiLanguage. Reproduced: ParseText({"UiLanguage":"en"}) and ({"ConfigVersion":2,"UiLanguage":"en"}) both give "vi". Real legacy files never had that key, so impact is limited to hand-written/shared snippets and Import. Remaining checks fine: version bump, blank language -> auto, null Actions/Shortcuts defaulted, idempotent (Migrate_Idempotent). See finding N-core-io-F07.
Null validator rejected; stateless afterwards. Test: NullValidator_ThrowsArgumentNullException.

Reports (never throws) for null Shortcuts, blank mandatory, invalid key name, null/blank action; optional blanks skipped; duplicates detected on canonical values case-insensitively across shortcuts and actions (Return = Enter). Conservative: Ctrl-modified shortcuts (Undo, OpenFolder) clash with a plain key of the same name. Tests: SettingsValidatorTests, SettingsValidatorRobustnessTests (Fuzz_ConflictOracle).
Lambda item => item.Value is the GroupBy key selector over canonical values; paired with OrdinalIgnoreCase comparer.
Lambda group => group.Count() > 1 finds the first duplicated key; ordering follows insertion so the reported conflict is deterministic.
Lambda item => item.Name joins the clashing binding names for the message; names are user-visible text only.

Builds alias->canonical map with OrdinalIgnoreCase; canonical names map to themselves to fix casing; indexer assignment so duplicate alias keys cannot throw; frozen for lookups. Test: AliasPairs_AllSameKey (verifies against WPF Key enum in App tests).
Trim, blank -> "", alias -> canonical (case-insensitive), unknown names returned trimmed; idempotent (Canonicalize_IsIdempotent). Null-safe.

Canonicalises every writable string property of ShortcutMappings and each action shortcut in place (mutates the caller's object, as Save documents); null Actions and null entries tolerated (CanonicalizeAll_NoActionsList_StillCanonicalisesTheShortcuts); null Shortcuts skipped.
Ordinal membership in OptionalNames; null name returns false. Tests exercised through the validator/normalizer suites.
Returns a fresh ShortcutMappings with defaults (no shared mutable instance). Tests: Defaults_* across settings test files.

Function: IFileSystem.bool TryCopyNew(string source, string destination, CopyCreationProof proof) (default interface method)
Rationale: New default interface method: ThrowIfNull(proof), returns false if the destination exists, else Copy then MarkCreated only after Copy returned (non-atomic; documented for fakes). Failure before/inside Copy leaves proof unmarked so callers never claim a foreign file. Covered by FileSystemCollisionContractTests and CopyForeignDestinationTests (R01 fix).
CopyCreationProof.DestinationCreated reads a volatile bool; safe to read from another thread.

MarkCreated sets the volatile flag; one-way (never reset), so a proof reused across calls would stay true: callers create one per copy (checked in FileActionService/RecoveryRetryService call sites by name only, outside this shard).

Function: PhysicalFileSystem.public bool TryCopyNew(string source, string destination, CopyCreationProof proof)
Rationale: R01 remedy: File.Copy (COPY_FILE_FAIL_IF_EXISTS) and MarkCreated only after it returns, so a throw never claims ownership (missing source with a foreign destination leaves the foreign file unclaimed); destination-exists IOException (80/183) returns false unless the destination is a directory, which rethrows. A partial file left by a failed physical copy is deliberately not claimed (left for Recovery). Tests: PhysicalFileSystemTryCopyNewTests, PhysicalIoMutationGapTests.TryCopyNew_SourceMissing_..., CopyForeignDestinationTests.

Function: CountingFileSystem.public bool TryCopyNew(string source, string destination, CopyCreationProof proof)
Rationale: Forwards the proof overload to the inner file system so ownership evidence from the physical implementation survives the metrics decorator (a decorator that dropped the proof would make every copy look unowned). Covered by FileSystemWrapperForwardingTests (Integration.Tests).
